subject: Hosted API pricing — runway bands, $/1M target, and burst headroom
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@orchidlabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing — runway bands, $/1M target, and burst headroom

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick write-up of what we heard + what we need to move to a formal estimate: 

Recap of what Orchid signaled on the call:
- Expected steady-state monthly token volume: 30–50M tokens (primary production use).
- Peak instantaneous TPS: ~110–140 qps during business hour spikes (99th percentile target).
- Topology: single-region US production today, planning a second region late H2 for DR.
- Data classification: low-sensitivity PII; must adhere to SOC 2 and audit log retention requests.

Commercial asks from your side:
- Target unit economics: <$45 per 1M tokens to make the integrations viable for user-facing features.
- Budget band for hosted: $35k–$60k / month depending on committed runrate and SLA.

What we need from you to get a binding quote and SLA options:
1) A representative week of traffic (CSV or JSON) with timestamps — this lets us size burst headroom and propose the right reserved slab.
2) Confirmation if you need 99th-pct latency SLOs at current peak TPS (we can propose both 95th and 99th options).
3) Any procurement timelines for PO or contract review.

Next steps I propose:
- You share the week-of-traffic export (or tell us when procurement can talk terms) — ideally by Mon 6/26.
- We run it through our batching/sla model and come back with: (a) two price paths (committed monthly slab vs. flexible PAYG + burst); (b) recommended peak TPS headroom and fallback model variants.

Attachments: I referenced an example token-runway CSV in the call — please attach your export if available.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: token_runway_example.csv (CSV, 4KB)

On Thu, Jun 21, 2028 at 2:05 PM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick write-up of what we heard + what we need to move to a formal estimate: 
> 
> Recap of what Orchid signaled on the call:
> - Expected steady-state monthly token volume: 30–50M tokens (primary production use).
> - Peak instantaneous TPS: ~110–140 qps during business hour spikes (99th percentile target).

Thanks Vanessa — quick clarifications from our side: 
- The 30–50M is conservative for Q3; if we move beyond pilot we'll likely push toward the 45–70M range in Q4. For the quote please include an escalator option for +50% volume.
- Peak TPS: 120 qps is our current realistic peak; short spikes (3–6 minutes) can hit ~200 qps during large import jobs, but those are off-peak. We're mainly worried about 1–3 minute spikes during launches.
- Budget: procurement asked to target $40/1M or better for committed slabs; they can stretch to $55k/month for a 6–12 month committed volume with SLA.

I've attached a scrubbed week of traffic (timestamps + token counts) and a short procurement note.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Integrations, Orchid Labs
alex@orchidlabs.com | (617) 555-0133

Attachments: orchid_week_of_traffic_202806.csv (CSV, 28KB); orchid_procurement_note.pdf (PDF, 12KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@orchidlabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — runway bands, $/1M target, and burst headroom

Alex — perfect, thanks for the traffic export and the procurement note. Quick responses inline and a proposed cadence: 

- Volume escalator: we'll include a +50% step function in the commitment table (base slab / +50% slab / +100% slab) so you can see per-1M price at each band.
- Spiky imports: for short 3–6 minute bursts that hit ~200 qps we recommend a hybrid approach: reserved slab sized for 99th-pct production (~120 qps) + short burst credits that auto-burst to a higher-capacity tier for up to 10 minutes. That preserves predictable unit economics while avoiding sustained over-provisioning.
- Target price: we'll design an option that gets to $40/1M at a 12-month committed slab near the 50M+ band. PAYG will be ~10–30% higher depending on burst usage.
- SLA tiers: 95th-pct latency SLO included by default; 99th SLO add-on with higher reserved capacity and a 1.5x delta on monthly commit to guarantee headroom.

Action items and timeline:
1) Karthik — can you run the attached CSV through the traffic modeling pipeline and produce: (a) reserved slab recommendation (monthly tokens + 99th qps sizing), (b) estimated $/1M at 3 commitment levels, and (c) recommended burst credits and pricing? Can you aim for Monday EOD 6/26?
2) Alex — once we have Karthik's model, we'll share a 1-page pricing summary and an initial term sheet for procurement to review.
3) Marissa — I may need a quick legal/pricing pre-check before sending the term sheet; can you spare 30 minutes Tue 6/27?

Thanks both — I'll produce the draft pricing summary and link to the Drive doc once Karthik has the numbers.

Best,
Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
Attachment stubs: orchid_week_of_traffic_202806.csv (CSV, 28KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — runway bands, $/1M target, and burst headroom

On Fri, Jun 22, 2028 at 8:34 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — perfect, thanks for the traffic export and the procurement note. Quick responses inline and a proposed cadence: 

I've kicked off a modeling run against the CSV. Preliminary notes: 
- Baseline recommendation: reserve for ~45M tokens/month to hit target $40/1M at a 12-month commit; that maps to ~120 99th-pct qps in our simulation.
- Burst profile: allow 10 minutes/day of elevated capacity to cover 200 qps spikes using transient credits — estimated additional cost is ~8–12% on top of committed slab if spikes occur at the frequency in the sample.
- Alternatives: PAYG + burst will land around $52–$60/1M given the sampled burst frequency.

I'll have the full sizing sheet and the three-band pricing table uploaded to Drive by EOD Monday 6/26 and will post the link here.

Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
